stem:
Kabir wants a fair test of whether warm or cold conditions change how fast water moves up a plant. He has two similar cut celery stalks, two glasses of the same red-coloured water, and can place one glass in a warm place and one in a cool place.

Answer both parts.

parts.text: Which claim correctly designs that fair test?

options.text: Use comparable stalks, the same coloured water, and change only temperature; judge the faster condition by which stalk shows the red colour higher sooner.
Use a short stalk in warm water and a long stalk in cold water; whichever turns red at the top first shows the faster temperature condition.
The stalk that turns red later transports water faster.
A stalk without flowers cannot be used to test water transport speed.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A fair test keeps stalk length and dye the same and varies only temperature; earlier rise of colour shows faster water transport, and flowers are not required.

teacher.key_rationale: Fair test: comparable twigs, same dye, vary only temperature, compare how quickly colour appears.
